name: What is the difference between a kitchen expansion and an open-concept conversion?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a kitchen expansion and an open-concept conversion?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between a kitchen expansion and an open-concept conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: A kitchen expansion increases the actual size of the kitchen, usually by extending the footprint or reassigning nearby space. An open-concept conversion, by contrast, changes the relationship between rooms by removing walls or openings so the kitchen feels larger and more connected. In practice, many Los Angeles projects combine both approaches. A homeowner might remove a wall to open the kitchen to a family room and also add a bump-out for more prep area or storage. The distinction matters because it changes the budget, engineering needs, and permit complexity. Open-concept work often raises structural questions if walls are load-bearing, while expansions may require foundation and exterior envelope work. This query deserves more precise content because many pages use the terms loosely, leaving searchers confused. A useful answer should explain the design intent, structural impact, and common reasons people choose one approach over the other.
acceptedAnswer.description: A kitchen expansion adds more square footage to the kitchen, while an open-concept conversion removes barriers between the kitchen and nearby rooms. An expansion creates more physical space; an open-concept conversion changes how existing space is connected. Some projects include both.
